summaries.economy: Inflation is accelerating sharply, complicating the new Fed chair's policy path. Bond yields hit their highest levels in nearly a year this week. Markets are now pricing a rate hike as more likely than a cut.
summaries.economy_long: Inflation accelerated to 3.8% in April, with professional forecasters projecting 6% by Q2. The Strait of Hormuz closure has driven oil above $109, pushing 30-year Treasury yields past 5.1%. Incoming Fed Chair Warsh's first FOMC decision on June 16–17 is now the pivotal near-term policy event.
summaries.industries: Amazon launched 30-minute delivery, pressuring last-mile warehouse demand further. Small-bay industrial vacancy remains below 5% nationally. AI tools are reshaping supply chain operations for industrial tenants.
summaries.industries_long: Small-bay industrial vacancy sits below 5%; investor capital continues flowing into multitenant and infill product. Amazon's 30-minute delivery expansion is intensifying demand for dense, last-mile warehouse infrastructure. Watch Blackstone's $1.75 billion data center REIT as it begins deploying capital across its $25 billion target pipeline.
summaries.logistics: Supply chains are under severe stress from the Strait of Hormuz closure. Fuel costs, spot rates, and carrier capacity are all tightening fast. Companies are racing to build inventory, driving urgent demand for warehouse space.
summaries.logistics_long: Hormuz closure is straining global supply chains, with diesel at $5.64 and spot rates near record highs. Fuel shocks, tightening trucking capacity, and accelerating inventory stockpiling are driving simultaneous cost and demand pressure. Watch the C.H. Robinson ruling: rising broker insurance costs and tighter carrier vetting will further squeeze available capacity.
summaries.policy: Trade policy remains unsettled despite a cautious US-China truce extension. Tariff refunds are flowing, but customs enforcement is intensifying sharply. Quartz import tariffs now threaten supply chains for California distributors.
summaries.policy_long: US-China trade policy is stabilizing under a three-year strategic framework, with tariffs holding at 47.5%. Tariff refunds, customs enforcement, and sector-specific petitions are reshaping the compliance landscape for importers. Watch Trump's decision on quartz tariffs and the November expiration of the US-China trade truce.
summaries.bottom_line: The Strait of Hormuz closure, accelerating inflation, and rising tariff enforcement are hitting industrial operators simultaneously. Companies are racing to build inventory, and that urgency is filling warehouse space fast.
